method: Each move is the token's price change relative to Bitcoin over the same days, from Binance perpetual-futures daily candles where the token trades there (else Binance spot, else CoinGecko), using the price at 00:00 UTC (day 0 is the unlock date, so its price is from before the unlock). CoinGecko's own history was wrong for some tokens on some days, so it is only the last resort. Grades use the same rules as the live page, with size, trading volume and circulating supply taken from CoinGecko as they were the day before each unlock. Monthly tranches of the same token overlap: the 30 days before one unlock include the 14 days after the previous one. 'Beyond normal' compares each unlock's three weeks (7 days before to 14 after) with the token's own average three-week drift against Bitcoin over the whole year, so a token that slides all year is not blamed on its unlock. For tokens that unlock every month that average already contains unlocks, so this measure understates their effect. Dollar moves are plain USD price changes. Short results are the % gained by shorting at the entry day's price and covering at the exit day's price, before fees and funding; 'worst move against you' is the highest daily close while the short was open, so intraday spikes were worse. 'Edge over random timing' subtracts the median result of shorting the same token for the same number of days starting on every day of the year. Ranges are 90% ranges for the median, found by resampling whole tokens (not single unlocks), because one token's monthly tranches move together.
